name: Raycast
description:
## A command center for everyday Mac work

Raycast lets you open applications, find files, run commands, and complete common tasks from one keyboard-driven interface. Open it with a shortcut, start typing, and choose the action you need without moving through several menus or applications.

## What Raycast does

Raycast combines an application launcher with productivity tools such as clipboard history, snippets, quick links, window management, calculations, notes, and AI commands. Its extension system adds commands for third-party services and lets developers build workflows that run directly inside Raycast.

## What you can do

- Launch applications and search for files
- Reuse previously copied text through clipboard history
- Save frequently used text as snippets
- Open websites and searches with quick links
- Arrange windows with built-in window management commands
- Install extensions for services such as GitHub, Linear, Notion, and Spotify
- Create custom commands and extensions
- Use AI for writing, questions, and application-specific actions

## Where it fits

Raycast is useful for people who prefer controlling their Mac from the keyboard and want several small productivity tools in one place. It can replace a basic application launcher while also reducing the need for separate clipboard, snippet, window-management, and quick-search utilities.
previewImageAltText: Raycast command interface and product branding

name: Swish
tagline: The missing gesture layer for macOS.
description:
## Window management built around gestures

Swish lets you arrange and control windows using trackpad gestures. You can swipe, pinch, or tap over a window's title bar to move, resize, minimize, close, or maximize it without dragging it across the screen.

## What Swish does

Swish adds gesture-based window controls to macOS. Its gestures work across window title bars, Dock icons, and the menu bar, giving you quick access to common window and application actions.

It supports grid-based layouts for placing several windows on the same display. You can also move windows between displays and Spaces, resize neighboring windows together, and use keyboard controls when a trackpad gesture is not convenient.

## What you can do

- Snap windows into 2×2, 3×2, and 3×3 layouts
- Minimize, close, maximize, or enter full screen with gestures
- Move windows between monitors and macOS Spaces
- Resize adjacent windows together
- Control applications through Dock and menu-bar gestures
- Use Arrow, WASD, IJKL, or Dvorak-oriented keyboard controls
- Enable or disable individual gestures
- Learn the controls through the included interactive tutorial

## Where it fits

Swish is useful for people who regularly work with several windows and prefer using a MacBook trackpad or Magic Trackpad. It provides a direct way to organize windows because actions are performed on the windows themselves. Compared with window managers centered around keyboard shortcuts or drag-to-edge snapping, Swish focuses primarily on gestures while retaining keyboard controls when they are useful.
tags: Keyboard & shortcuts, Mouse & gestures, Window management
previewImageAltText: Swish gesture-based window management on macOS

name: Superwhisper
tagline: Turn your voice into polished text.
description:
## Write in any application using your voice

Superwhisper lets you dictate wherever you can type. Press a shortcut, speak naturally, and the finished text is inserted into the active application with punctuation and formatting already applied.

## What Superwhisper does

Superwhisper combines speech recognition with configurable writing modes. Voice mode produces a faithful transcript, while AI-assisted modes can remove filler words, correct grammar, organize a longer thought, or adapt the result for an email, message, document, or prompt.

The application supports both local and cloud speech models. Local models allow compatible Macs to process dictation without an internet connection, while cloud models provide another option for speed and accuracy.

## What you can do

- Dictate into email, chat, notes, documents, and development tools
- Create custom modes for different writing styles and formats
- Add names, abbreviations, and specialist terms to a vocabulary
- Transcribe audio and video files
- Record meetings and produce organized notes
- Dictate and translate more than 100 languages
- Use local speech models on compatible Macs
- Start dictation through configurable keyboard shortcuts

## Where it fits

Superwhisper is useful for people who write substantial amounts of text and want more control than standard macOS dictation provides. Its custom modes make it especially suitable for switching between emails, messages, long-form writing, meeting notes, and prompts without manually reformatting every transcript.

name: Wispr Flow
description:
## Dictate wherever you would normally type

Wispr Flow lets you speak into text fields across macOS. Hold the dictation shortcut, say what you want to write, and release it to place the finished text into the active application.

## What Wispr Flow does

Flow turns speech into formatted text rather than returning a word-for-word transcript. It removes filler words, adds punctuation, handles corrections made while speaking, and can structure lists, paragraphs, messages, and emails automatically.

Flow also learns the words and phrases you use. Its dictionary helps with names and specialist terminology, while snippets let you speak a short cue to insert a longer saved block of text.

## What you can do

- Dictate into any application with a text field
- Correct yourself naturally while speaking
- Create paragraphs and numbered lists by voice
- Add names and technical terms to a personal dictionary
- Insert saved text using spoken snippet commands
- Change or summarize text with AI commands
- Dictate in more than 100 languages
- Use hands-free dictation for longer writing sessions

## Where it fits

Wispr Flow is useful for people who want voice input to work consistently across email, messaging, documents, browsers, and development tools. It focuses on producing text that is ready to send with minimal editing, making it suitable for frequent short messages as well as longer drafts.
previewImageAltText: Wispr Flow voice dictation product preview

name: Mole
tagline: Native Mac utility for cleanup, software, and status.
description:
## Keep storage and system tools in one application

Mole lets you review storage, remove unnecessary files, uninstall applications, run maintenance tasks, and monitor Mac hardware from a native interface. It brings several jobs that are often handled by separate utilities into one application.

## What Mole does

Mole organizes its tools into focused areas for cleaning, software management, optimization, disk analysis, and live system status. Scans show what can be removed before anything is deleted, while the software section can find application leftovers, startup items, and available updates.

Its status tools display current CPU, memory, GPU, disk, network, battery, temperature, and fan information. A menu-bar view keeps selected measurements available without leaving the active application.

## What you can do

- Review and remove supported cache and temporary files
- Uninstall applications together with related files
- Manage startup items and application updates
- Run common macOS maintenance operations
- Analyze disk usage through a visual storage map
- Monitor hardware and resource usage
- View status information from the menu bar
- Adjust supported fan-control modes

## Where it fits

Mole is useful for people who want a visual, Mac-native utility for both storage cleanup and system monitoring. It can reduce the need to maintain separate applications for uninstalling software, mapping disk usage, checking hardware statistics, and running routine maintenance.
tags: Menu bar, Storage & cleanup, System monitoring
previewImageAltText: Mole Mac cleanup and system utility interface

name: LookAway
tagline: Smart Break Reminder App for Mac.
description:
## Take regular breaks without managing a timer

LookAway lets you schedule short screen breaks and receive reminders while you work. It runs from the menu bar and handles the timing automatically, helping you look away from the display, blink more often, and change posture during long sessions.

## What LookAway does

LookAway places break reminders over the screen at intervals you choose. The reminders are designed to remain visible long enough to encourage a real pause while avoiding unnecessary interruptions during calls, videos, games, or other situations where a break would be poorly timed.

Break schedules, reminder styles, sounds, and appearance can be adjusted to match different working routines. You can also postpone or skip a reminder when you need to finish the current task.

## What you can do

- Schedule recurring screen breaks
- Add separate reminders for blinking and posture
- Customize break duration and frequency
- Pause reminders during calls, videos, or selected applications
- Postpone or skip an upcoming break
- Choose reminder sounds and visual styles
- Control LookAway from the menu bar
- Sync supported reminders with an iPhone through LookAway Mirror

## Where it fits

LookAway is useful for people who spend long periods reading, writing, designing, coding, or working in a browser. It provides more structure than a basic timer because it accounts for what is happening on the Mac and can avoid interrupting activities where a full-screen reminder would be disruptive.
previewImageAltText: LookAway break reminder interface on macOS

name: Mimestream
tagline: Made for Mac. Optimized for Gmail.
description:
## Use Gmail through a native Mac application

Mimestream lets you manage Gmail accounts from a macOS interface while retaining Gmail features such as categories, labels, server-side filters, aliases, and search. It connects through the Gmail API rather than treating Gmail as a generic IMAP account.

## What Mimestream does

Mimestream combines Gmail's organization with familiar macOS controls. Inbox categories keep promotional and social messages separate, colored labels remain available, and server-side filters can be created or edited without opening Gmail in a browser.

The composer supports aliases, reusable templates, Markdown shortcuts, code formatting, mentions, undo send, and send-and-archive. Calendar invitations can be viewed alongside calendar availability before responding.

## What you can do

- Manage multiple Google and Gmail accounts
- Use Gmail categories, labels, search, and filters
- Write from configured Gmail aliases
- Create reusable email templates
- Respond to calendar invitations with schedule context
- Format messages with Markdown shortcuts and code blocks
- Use keyboard shortcuts, swipe gestures, and multiple windows
- Access notifications and account controls from the menu bar

## Where it fits

Mimestream is useful for people who rely on Gmail but prefer a dedicated Mac application over a browser tab. It is particularly relevant when Gmail-specific organization and search are important, because those features are integrated directly instead of being approximated through a general-purpose email protocol.
previewImageAltText: Mimestream native Gmail client for macOS

name: Klack
description:
## Add mechanical keyboard sounds to any Mac keyboard

Klack lets you hear a responsive mechanical-keyboard sound whenever you type. It runs as a menu-bar application and plays recorded switch sounds with separate feedback for pressing and releasing a key.

## What Klack does

Klack adds audio feedback without requiring a mechanical keyboard. Different switch profiles change the character of the sound, while randomized pitch keeps repeated keystrokes from sounding exactly the same. Spatial audio places the feedback around the typing position for a more natural result.

The application responds immediately to typing and can follow changes in audio output, including supported headphones. Its controls stay in the menu bar so the sound can be changed or muted without opening a large application window.

## What you can do

- Choose between multiple recorded keyboard-switch sounds
- Hear separate sounds for key-down and key-up actions
- Adjust the tone through a tuning pad
- Enable randomized pitch variation
- Use immersive spatial audio
- Control the application from the menu bar
- Automate sleep and wake behavior
- Review typing usage statistics

## Where it fits

Klack is useful for people who enjoy audible typing feedback but use a MacBook keyboard, Magic Keyboard, or quiet external keyboard. It is a focused customization utility rather than a typing assistant: it does not change what is entered, but changes how typing feels and sounds.
previewImageAltText: Klack application preview from the Mac App Store

name: IINA
tagline: The modern media player for macOS.
description:
## Play video and audio in a Mac-native interface

IINA lets you open a wide range of local media files and online streams in an interface designed specifically for macOS. It uses the mpv playback engine while providing native controls, menus, gestures, and system integrations.

## What IINA does

IINA handles common and less common video and audio formats without requiring a separate codec pack. Playback controls include chapters, playlists, subtitles, speed adjustment, video filters, thumbnail previews, and picture-in-picture. A dedicated music mode provides a smaller interface for audio playback.

The player can also open supported online media through browser extensions and optional plugins. Advanced users can customize keyboard mappings, mouse and trackpad gestures, interface layouts, mpv settings, and scripts.

## What you can do

- Play most common video and audio file formats
- Watch video in macOS Picture in Picture
- Search for and manage subtitles
- Preview positions in a video with thumbnail navigation
- Use a compact interface for music playback
- Open supported online streams and playlists
- Customize playback controls and interface layouts
- Extend the player through plugins and mpv configuration

## Where it fits

IINA is useful for people who need broader format support than QuickTime Player while still wanting an application that looks and behaves like a modern Mac app. Its default interface is approachable for ordinary playback, while mpv settings, plugins, and custom controls provide depth for advanced use.
previewImageAltText: IINA media player interface on macOS

name: Dayflow
tagline: Automatic work journal & AI time tracker for Mac.
description:
## Build a timeline of your work automatically

Dayflow lets you review what you worked on without starting timers or writing activity notes throughout the day. It observes screen activity on your Mac and turns it into a chronological timeline with readable summaries.

## What Dayflow does

Dayflow analyzes short segments of screen activity to identify the work taking place inside an application, not only which application was open. A browser session can therefore be described as research, documentation, communication, or entertainment based on the visible context.

The resulting timeline supports daily standups, weekly reviews, focus analysis, and questions about previous work. Recordings, timeline data, and the application database are stored locally by default, and you choose which local or cloud AI provider performs the analysis.

## What you can do

- Create an automatic timeline of daily activity
- Review summaries of completed work
- Generate daily standup notes
- Compare focus and distraction patterns across a week
- Ask questions about previous work sessions
- Export timeline entries as Markdown
- Use local models through Ollama or LM Studio
- Set storage limits and remove older recordings automatically

## Where it fits

Dayflow is useful for people who want a work journal or time record but repeatedly forget to operate manual timers. It is especially helpful for reconstructing a day, preparing status updates, reviewing focus patterns, or remembering which tasks occupied a particular block of time.
previewImageAltText: Dayflow automatic work journal and timeline preview
